summary.one_liner: Void is an open-source, VS Code-based desktop code editor with built-in AI agents, now deprecated and no longer accepting contributions.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Void as a fork of the VS Code repository that adds AI agents working on a codebase, change checkpoints and visualization, and support for bringing any model or hosting models locally. It says messages go directly to providers without the project retaining user data. The README notes the project is deprecated and no longer accepts contributions, and points to a list of newer Void forks and to old releases for download. It also serves as a reference for forking VS Code, mentioning React + Tailwind mounted in the build pipeline, copied GitHub Actions for packaging and auto-update, a custom AI provider layer supporting autocomplete (FIM), and services such as EditCodeService for streaming diffs and VoidModelService for background file edits. Supporting docs referenced include a codebase guide and a contribution guide.
use_cases: Reference architecture for forking VS Code
Using AI agents on a local codebase
Reviewing and checkpointing AI-made code changes
Connecting a custom or local LLM to an editor
Studying VS Code extension and build pipeline customization
how_to_run: To download an old version, see the Releases page referenced in the README
See the Void Forks list referenced in the README for newer forks
notable: Project is deprecated; README points users to newer community forks
Forked from VS Code with React and Tailwind compiled into the build pipeline
Custom AI provider code supporting autocomplete (FIM) and custom tool tags
EditCodeService streams diffs token by token; VoidModelService syncs OS files with editor buffers
Sends messages directly to model providers without retaining data, per README
caveats: Deprecated and no longer accepting contributions
Desktop app only; the README does not describe other platforms
Developing your own version requires the VS Code fork build setup described in separate guides
